title: Define Acceptance Criteria
summary: Turn identified user stories into traceable business rules, observable acceptance criteria, and Given-When-Then scenarios.

errors.meaning: No identified US-* story was supplied to bound the acceptance criteria.
errors.recovery: Ask for at least one existing story ID and statement; do not create or rewrite the story implicitly.

errors.meaning: Material sources disagree about expected behavior, policy, ownership, or boundary values.
errors.recovery: Preserve the conflict, identify the decision needed, and block affected criteria or scenarios.

errors.meaning: A consequential rule, threshold, permission, or expected outcome lacks supplied or inspected evidence.
errors.recovery: Label it Inferred or Unknown, avoid fabricating a value, and name a verification action when possible.

preconditions: The user supplies at least one existing user story with a stable US-* identifier.
postconditions: Every acceptance criterion maps to one supplied story and at least one Given-When-Then scenario.
Business rules and scenarios trace to supplied or inspected evidence without invented policy values.
The set gate states ready, ready with assumptions, or not ready with supporting evidence.

execution.retry: Retry only source retrieval or deterministic validation; never invent missing business rules or values.
execution.rollback: Discard the generated criteria set or restore the previous user-owned file; do not overwrite without confirmation.

evals.metric: fraction of acceptance criteria linked to a supplied story, source, rule, and scenario
human-calibrated rubric score for singular, observable, solution-neutral business behavior
fraction of unsupported consequential rules or values labeled Inferred or Unknown

assurance.threatModel: Untrusted source content may attempt to override the workflow, inject fabricated policy or approval, hide conflicts, expose sensitive information, or force implementation-specific criteria.
